newsitem.title: FRANCE: Troubled Air Liberte put in legal administration.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Air Liberte put in legal administration.

text.p: French airline Air Liberte said a court had put the private carrier under legal administration on Thursday after it defaulted on payments, giving it six months to try and haul itself out of trouble.
Chairman Lotfi Belhassine said airline employees had agreed to put two months' wages towards an injection of capital to try to haul set the carrier back on course.
"We decided unanimously to tackle our troubles through solidarity," Belhassine told reporters.

"We're going to increase our capital. All the staff present at the general meeting voted -- two months wages invested in the company over 18 months. As chairman, I will take part in the capital increase," he told reporters.
A spokeswoman for the airline confirmed that a salvage plan had been drawn up which involved shedding 285 jobs and focusing on medium- and short-haul flights.
Sixty percent of the planned 100 million French franc ($19.44 million) capital increase would come from staff, she said.
The airline lost 160 million francs in the first six months of this year and one newspaper said this week that Air Liberte's losses could total 600 million by the end of 1996.
Belhassine has blamed the airline's woes on a price war and said preferential treatment for state-owned Air France from the Paris airport authorities has also taken a toll.
Planes belonging to the airline were plagued by even more immediate diffiiculties on Thursday getting refuelling from suppliers worried about getting paid, TF1 television said.
Another private airline, AOM, said in a statement it was cancelling from midnight a reciprocal arrangement under which tickets for either airline were valid on the other. ($1=5.145 French Franc)
